S1.mechanism: Daily-reset leveraged/inverse funds rebalance toward their targets late in the session, which can extend a large move.

S2.mechanism: Mandated late reset selling on big down days may create an overnight rebound.

S3.mechanism: Late closing imbalance restrictions can force liquidity providers to absorb excess supply; use a five-minute bar proxy, not an imbalance feed.

S4.mechanism: Attention-driven opening orders can create a temporary dislocation that liquidity providers unwind later in the morning.

S5.mechanism: Creation-unit order deadlines concentrate ETF authorized participant hedging and arbitrage near the close, potentially reducing wide tracking gaps.

S6.mechanism: Options dealers rehedge before the close; a large range and its current location are bar-only stand-ins for pressure and reversal.

S7.mechanism: Dealers who absorb late sell orders can earn back an inventory discount overnight.

S8.mechanism: Institutional execution programs repeat the same intraday time buckets on multiple days.

S9.mechanism: Higher overnight margin and stock-borrow fees push intraday arbitrageurs to cut risk near the close.

S10.mechanism: A shift in risk budgets and sentiment over the weekend may reverse some Friday pressure.

S11.mechanism: Financially constrained liquidity providers pull back amid sharp intraday selling, leaving a possible rebound premium.

S12.mechanism: Portfolio window dressing can force sales near equity month/quarter ends that unwind on the next session.
